patients.summary: High school history teacher with long-standing hypertension and type 2 diabetes who joined in 2019 and was steady on lisinopril and metformin for years, with untreated mixed hyperlipidemia. In late 2025 he developed acute poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis, then thiazide-induced hypokalemia in February 2026; both settled, and amlodipine was added.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
50 y/o man transferring care; his last practice is closing its panel and he wanted a doctor he can text. Teaches history at the high school, starts back next week.

HTN for roughly six years, always on lisinopril, currently 20 mg once a day. Type 2 DM picked up about three and a half years ago on routine labs, metformin 1000 mg twice daily since, no lows, no GI trouble now. Has never been on insulin. No home glucose checks lately. Prior records requested.

No surgeries. NKDA.
Family: father with type 2 diabetes from age 58. Mother has high blood pressure and high cholesterol. Maternal grandfather had an MI at 65.
Social: has never used tobacco. A beer or two on weekends. Walks most evenings.

ROS negative, including vision, chest symptoms, urinary symptoms, foot numbness.

Exam: well, pleasant. BP and HR per vitals. BMI 30. Fundi not dilated. Thyroid normal size. Heart with regular rhythm, no murmur. Lungs without crackles or wheeze. Abdomen soft. Feet: skin intact, monofilament felt at all sites, dorsalis pedis palpable both sides. Legs without swelling.

A/P
1. Hypertension: at goal on lisinopril 20. Continue. BMP today.
2. Type 2 diabetes: A1c, fasting glucose, urine microalbumin today. Continue metformin 1000 BID. Eye exam yearly, he will book with his optometrist.
3. Lipids drawn today as part of the baseline.
4. Prevention: Tdap given. Hep C and HIV screening today, he agreed. Due for colonoscopy at 50, referral placed to GI. PHQ-2 negative.

Return in about 6 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Derek, your baseline labs are back. Kidney function, blood counts and the urine protein test are all normal. A1c is in a good range for someone on metformin. Hep C and HIV screens are negative. Talk soon.

documents.title: Colonoscopy Report (outside GI)
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology group. Procedure date 11/19/2019.
Indication: first screening colonoscopy, age 50, no family history of colon cancer.
Medications: metformin, lisinopril. Allergies: NKDA.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care.
Prep: good, Boston-type score not recorded; adequate for polyps over 5 mm.
Findings: scope advanced to the cecum, appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve photographed. Withdrawal time 9 minutes. Mucosa normal throughout. No polyps, masses or diverticula seen. Retroflexion in the rectum normal.
Impression: normal screening exam.
Recommendation: next colonoscopy in 10 years.
Copy to referring primary care physician.

documents.title: Annual Physical Examination
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, on school vacation. Mostly here to keep the diabetes on track. No complaints at all, sleeping fine, energy fine.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily. NKDA.
FH: father developed type 2 diabetes at 58.
SH: nonsmoker. Social drinker, weekends only.

Vitals: BP 132/85, HR 78. BMI 30.
General: comfortable, no distress.
HEENT, neck: normal; no thyroid enlargement or nodes.
CV: S1 S2 normal, no murmur.
Resp: clear throughout.
Abd: soft, nontender, no organomegaly.
Ext: no swelling. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses strong, skin healthy.
Neuro, skin: normal.
PHQ-2: 0.

Fasting labs drawn before the visit: glucose 126, A1c 6.5%. Lipids TC 210, HDL 35, LDL 145, TG 150.

A/P
- T2DM, controlled on metformin. Continue 1000 BID. Urine microalbumin pending.
- HTN on lisinopril 20, fine. Continue.
- Prevention: colonoscopy 2019 normal, Tdap 2019, Shingrix done, flu and COVID booster this fall. Eye exam got pushed; he will reschedule.
Follow up in about 6 months.

documents.author: PCP

Back to go over cholesterol and make sure the meds are working for him. Summer break started. No new symptoms of any kind. Takes metformin twice a day and lisinopril every morning, rarely misses.

Family history reviewed again: father with type 2 diabetes diagnosed at 58; mother with hypertension and high cholesterol; maternal grandfather had an MI at 65.
Nonsmoker. Weekend drinks, one or two.

BP 132/84.

Fasting labs from this morning: A1c 7.2% (up from 6.5 in December), glucose 154. TC 210, LDL 140, HDL 40, triglycerides 250.

Assessment
- Mixed hyperlipidemia: LDL and triglycerides both up, HDL low. Adding to the problem list.
- T2DM, A1c drifted up over six months.
- HTN stable on lisinopril.

Plan: we talked about cutting back refined carbs and the weekend beer, more walking now that school is out. I'll send him the dietitian handout. Same metformin and lisinopril. Recheck labs before a visit around the holidays.

events.reason: Follow-up; question about a lipid drug trial

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
53 y/o with HTN, T2DM, mixed hyperlipidemia. Feels well, nothing new to report. Compliant with metformin and lisinopril.

His main question today: a colleague forwarded him an ad for a study of an investigational cholesterol drug, randomized against placebo, and he wants to know if it is worth his time.

BP 132/84. Exam unremarkable: heart and lungs normal, abdomen benign, legs without swelling.

Labs 12/19 reviewed: A1c 7.2%, fasting glucose 154. TC 210, LDL 130, HDL 40, TG 250. Urine microalbumin normal.

Discussion re trial: went over what placebo-controlled means, that he might get the inactive pill for the length of the study, and what randomization protects against. Pointed out that the planned enrollment is small, so a single study like this can't tell us much on its own, though his participation would still be voluntary and closely monitored. Suggested he read the consent carefully and bring questions to the study team; happy to look at the consent with him. He will think it over.

Plan: same medications. Keep working on diet and walking. Physical in the spring or summer.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly exam. Doing well. No chest discomfort, shortness of breath, numbness in the feet, or vision change. Meds: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily.

Eye exam: went in October, no report ever reached us. He'll ask them again.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Pleasant, fit-appearing. Oropharynx clear, no adenopathy. Heart regular without murmur or gallop. Lungs clear to bases. Abdomen soft. Lower legs without swelling. Foot check: sensation normal to filament, pulses 2+, no skin breakdown.

PHQ-2 = 0.

Plan:
- Labs today: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, urine microalbumin.
- Pneumococcal: PCV20 today given diabetes.
- Colonoscopy 2019 normal, next 2029.
- Same meds. Diabetes check in about 6 months.

documents.title: Physical labs

documents.title: Acute Visit - Swelling and Dark Urine
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted over the weekend asking to be seen; first slot this morning.

HPI: 56 y/o teacher with HTN and type 2 diabetes, followed here, with two weeks of feeling wiped out, puffiness all over, and making less urine than usual. Over the same stretch his urine has gone a dark brown, like cola. Still taking metformin and lisinopril.

Exam: BP 160/100, well above his usual low 130s. Looks tired, not toxic. Heart regular, no rub. Lungs clear. 2+ pitting edema both lower legs to mid-shin.

UA in office: brown, 3+ protein, large blood, red cells too many to count, red cell casts on microscopy.

Labs back this afternoon: creatinine 2.8 (his baseline has been about 1.0), BUN 45, albumin 3.2. C3 62 (low), C4 24 (normal).

Assessment: acute nephritic syndrome with kidney injury, low C3 with normal C4. Most consistent with acute poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis. ASO titer sent and pending.

Plan:
- Urgent nephrology referral, front desk to push for an appointment within two weeks.
- Salt restriction, call or come in for shortness of breath, much less urine, or confusion.
- Called him at 4:45 pm with the afternoon results and plan. He understands.
- Will repeat labs per nephrology.

documents.title: ASO Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ASO titer 640 IU/mL (lab reference under 200), supports a recent strep infection and the post-strep diagnosis. Told Derek. Nephrology has him for Jan 7. Swelling unchanged, breathing fine. Reviewed warning signs again.

documents.title: Saw the kidney doctor
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Update: saw nephrology yesterday. She agreed it's the post-strep kind and said it usually settles on its own, so no biopsy for now. They drew more blood and want to see me again in about six weeks. Not sure if they send you anything, so passing it along.

documents.title: Re: Saw the kidney doctor
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks Derek, that's helpful. We haven't gotten their note yet. Glad the plan is to watch it. Keep the salt low and let me know if the swelling gets worse.

documents.title: Nephrology Visit Summary
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology office. Visit summary, date of service 02/18/2026. Sent in response to records request.

Diagnosis: acute poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis, recovering.
Interval: kidney function recovering on repeat labs. Swelling better. Blood pressure remains above goal.
Medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily. Allergies: none known.
Plan: start hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg once daily for blood pressure and residual edema. Continue lisinopril. Low-sodium diet. Return 3 months with labs.

medications.drug: potassium chloride 20 MEQ Extended Release Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 5 days

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia at 102 beats per minute. PR and QRS durations normal. Flattened T waves with prominent U waves. No ST elevation.
reports.conclusion: Sinus tachycardia; flattened T waves and U waves, consistent with hypokalemia.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Community hospital emergency department. Date of service 02/25/2026. Received by fax.

CC: feeling weak, heart racing, started about two hours before arrival.

HPI: 56M with hypertension and type 2 diabetes, recently treated for acute poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis by nephrology. Thiazide (hydrochlorothiazide) added one week ago. Today sudden generalized weakness and a fluttering heartbeat. No vomiting, no diarrhea, no laxatives. Adherent to metformin and lisinopril.

Allergies: NKDA.

Triage: BP 145/90, HR 102.
Exam: alert, oriented. Fine tremor of the outstretched hands. Heart tachycardic, regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Strength symmetric.

Labs: K 2.9, Na 140, Cl 100, HCO3 28, glucose 180, creatinine 1.0.
ECG: sinus tachycardia, flattened T waves, U waves.

MDM: symptomatic hypokalemia, most likely from the newly started thiazide. No GI losses. Kidney function at baseline.

ED course: potassium chloride 40 mEq by mouth, tolerated without nausea. Palpitations eased while here. Monitored on telemetry.

Disposition: discharged home. Stop hydrochlorothiazide. Potassium chloride 20 mEq ER twice daily for 5 days. See primary care in 2 to 3 days for repeat potassium. Return for worsening weakness, chest pain, or fainting.

documents.title: Call After ED Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called. Went to the ED yesterday afternoon with weakness and a racing heart; told his potassium was low, likely from the water pill the kidney doctor started last week. They stopped the water pill and gave him potassium tablets for 5 days. Feels better this morning, no palpitations. We do not have the ED record or a nephrology note about the new pill. Booked with PCP Monday 3/2 with a potassium check. ED instructions to return if symptoms recur reviewed.

events.reason: Follow-up after ED visit for low potassium

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after his ED visit 2/25. Story from him: nephrology started hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg on 2/18 (we never received that note), and a week later he had sudden weakness and palpitations. ED found potassium 2.9 with U waves on ECG, gave oral potassium, stopped the HCTZ, sent him home on KCl 20 mEq twice a day for 5 days. He finished the course yesterday. ED record not yet here either.

Today: no palpitations, no weakness, no tremor. Swelling much less than in December. Taking metformin 1000 BID and lisinopril 20 daily.

BP 142/88. Heart regular, normal rate. Lungs clear. No pitting edema today.

Potassium this morning 3.9.

A/P
1. Hypokalemia from thiazide: resolved on recheck. Thiazide stays off.
2. HTN, above goal off the thiazide: start amlodipine 5 mg daily. Continue lisinopril 20. Home readings, recheck at the physical.
3. Post-strep GN, recovering per patient report from nephrology. Records requested from nephrology and the ED today.
4. T2DM: continue metformin.

documents.title: Records Received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: ED physician record from 2/25 arrived by fax, indexed to chart and routed to PCP. Nephrology office says the 2/18 summary will be sent once their provider signs it.

documents.title: Nephrology Summary Received
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Nephrology visit summary from 2/18 finally in, after a second call. Confirms HCTZ 25 was their start for pressure and edema; already stopped after the ED visit. Their medication list predates amlodipine. Will let them know at his next nephrology visit via patient.

documents.title: Lab Draw

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
57 tomorrow. Yearly exam and a check on the kidneys after the winter.

Interval: post-strep GN in December, followed by nephrology; thiazide-related low potassium in February, resolved. Amlodipine added in March. He feels back to normal: energy good, no swelling, urine a normal color.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily. NKDA.

Vitals: BP 128/80. 
Exam: well-appearing. HEENT and neck normal. Heart regular, no murmur or rub. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No ankle or shin edema. Feet: sensation and pulses normal, skin intact. PHQ-2 0.

Labs 5/11: urinalysis negative for blood and protein. C3 112, back to normal. Kidney function and potassium normal. A1c in his usual range. Urine microalbumin normal. Lipids similar to prior.

A/P
- Post-streptococcal GN: resolved by labs and exam. Off the active list. He sees nephrology again in the late spring.
- HTN: at goal on lisinopril plus amlodipine. Continue both.
- T2DM: continue metformin.
- Health maintenance: eye exam due in August. Colonoscopy 2029. Fall vaccines.
Diabetes follow-up in about four months.

documents.title: Visit summary

documents.body: Good seeing you yesterday, Derek. Quick summary: your kidneys look fully recovered on the urine test and the complement level. Keep the amlodipine, lisinopril and metformin as they are. Book your eye exam for August, and we'll see you in September.
